content.comment_body: Hello, when I power on my [product_name], text messages appear on the display. Pressing ESC does not show the Menu (which I want to reach to start or stop the program, for instance). There is no response at all. The program is running and functions properly, but I am only able to open the MENU by connecting a PC. How can I access the menu directly from the module's panel? Best regards, [user_name]

To clarify, do you see the menu after stopping [product_name] with your PC? While in RUN mode, can you access other screens using the cursor keys? Is the message text activated via a pulse generator, or another method? Could you share your program so we can review it?

Thank you for your interest in my issue. Yes, when I stop the program on the [article_no] using my computer, I can access the display menu and start the program again. However, the display freezes once more, showing the text message. In the program, the text menu is activated by a constant HI input (not a pulse generator), which may be causing the problem. I am attaching the program that controls a heating system with a heat pump and water heaters. Sorry for its lack of structure. [user_name]
Hello again, I was unable to upload .lsc files, which is odd. Instead, I am sending a zip file. [user_name]
Menu access is disabled while a message text is displayed. First, use the cursor keys to navigate to the screen showing the clock or date, and then you will be able to press ESC to access the menu.
Thank you! That solved it. I appreciate your time and support! :) [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced trouble accessing the menu on a [product_name] module when a text message was visible—the ESC button did not respond. It was clarified that while a message text is displayed, menu access is restricted, and users must first switch screens using the cursor keys. The confusion stemmed from the message configuration within the program.
analysis.user_expectations: The user would like to access the menu directly from the module's display by pressing the ESC button, ideally without needing to change the currently shown screen.
